newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Salzburg Festival opens with tale from Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Salzburg Festival opens with tale from Ireland.

text.p: Austria's six-week Salzburg Festival opened on Sunday with music by Schubert, Mendelssohn and Salzburg's renowned son Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart.
The "Felsenreitschule", a theatre carved out of rock, was the setting for speeches by Austria's Chancellor Viktor Klima, President Thomas Klestil and the guest speaker, author Christoph Ransmayr.

An Austrian who lives in Ireland, Ransmayr left the formal speeches to the politicians and mesmerised the audience with a tale from the Irish coast. Conjuring up images of local life, he described music and dances on a windswept stage in West Cork.
Among those at the opening were Rita Suessmuth, President of the German Bundestag, and Slovenian Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek.
